name: theta-chain-features-parquet
notes: Node 2 of ADR-0265 on the Parquet tree (Amendment 3): the same features, parameters and outputs as run-theta-chain-features.json, fed by ParquetChainRows. The reader yields the chain symbol by symbol (a root's snapshots adjacent, dates ascending), which is what symbol_contiguous needs: the gzip unit reader's newest-snapshot-first order interleaves a root that spans snapshots with its neighbours and symbol_contiguous refuses it, so the gzip document could only run hold-everything. Features are identical to the gzip path on the same data (real-data parity on the landed ACMR snapshots, ADR-0265 Amendment 3). SAMPLE: symbols names three roots (AAPL, ABBV, ABNB); the real universe is the census output (run-theta-chain-census-parquet.json), frozen before any hypothesis runs. For the whole tree use run-theta-chain-panel.json, which writes date-partitioned panels root by root in bounded memory. READ-ONLY on /home/russell/data/thetadata/parquet-v2/options-tested/theta. SEALED PERIOD: end_before and sealed_from 2026-01-01 on the reader, end_before on the features node. RATE, EXCLUSIONS, STATUS and the feature definitions are those of run-theta-chain-features.json. Run from children/index_options: nice -n 10 python -m dskit.pipeline run configs/run-theta-chain-features-parquet.json --asof 2025-12-31.

outputs.notes: A new directory beside the other research runs; nothing is written under /home/russell/data/thetadata. Excluded from the identity hash.

chain.notes: The ThetaData daily chain from the Parquet export tree, restricted to the three sample roots (an isin predicate pushed into the scan: files and row groups of other roots are never decoded) and projected to the ten fields the features read. Rows arrive root by root with dates ascending, newest-acquired copy of a unit winning. Lazy, read-only.

features.notes: Targets are 30 days (plus or minus 7) and 90 days (plus or minus 14), the nearest listed expiry each; a day with none inside the tolerance emits no row for that target and is counted. min_forward_pairs 5 strikes quoted on both sides are needed for the parity forward. ATM is the strike nearest the forward in log terms among those with both sides usable inside a 5% band. The wing vols are at forward delta 0.25 in magnitude, linear in delta between the two bracketing strikes, null without a bracket. Open interest and volume are summed over the target's own expiry; the 5-session change looks back five sessions of the same root and is null past ten calendar days or when that expiry did not yet exist. RATE: the 3-month T-bill yield (percent, scaled by 0.01) of the last observation strictly BEFORE the quote date and at most 5 days earlier, used as a continuously compounded rate in the parity forward K + e^(rT)(C - P) and in Black-76; a day with no such observation is a no_rate row, never a zero rate. The bond-equivalent yield stands in for a continuous rate (a small approximation). STATUS: every requested target of every root-date leaves a row; status says ok, no_expiry, no_forward or no_rate.

params.source: one row per root, date and target DTE: ATM and 25-delta implied vols from NBBO mids on the parity forward, risk reversal, put-call IV spread, 30/90 term slope, straddle ratio, half-spread over premium, open interest and volume by side and the 5-session open-interest changes

table.notes: The feature table the H1 documents attach by (symbol, date, target_dte).

params.title: ThetaData chain day features (ADR-0265 node 2, Parquet tree)

counts.notes: evidence.md renders the exclusion counts (null, zero and crossed quotes, rows before each root's first bid) and the per-target emitted / no-expiry / no-forward counts.

rates_raw.notes: The FRED 3-month constant-maturity Treasury yield (DGS3MO, percent, dated by the observation date, '.' on a holiday) from the index_options onboarding root, read-only. The series runs to 2026-09, so the node below drops 2026 before anything joins it.

rates.notes: Sealed period and holidays: a 2026 observation never reaches the features node (which also refuses one), and a '.' (no print) is not a rate. The 2026 rows are parsed by the reader above and dropped here; the series is a macro rate, not option data.
